title: India's Net GST Collection Jumps 25.6% to Rs 2.03 Trillion in October
headline: India's Net GST Collection Jumps 25.6% to Rs 2.03 Trillion in October
subheadline: Gross collection rose 22.9% to Rs 2.31 trillion as import-linked tax revenue climbed 42%, according to government data reported on Sunday.
summary: Gross collection rose 22.9% to Rs 2.31 trillion as import-linked tax revenue climbed 42%, according to government data reported on Sunday.
excerpt: Gross collection rose 22.9% to Rs 2.31 trillion as import-linked tax revenue climbed 42%, according to government data reported on Sunday.
body:
• India's net GST collection rose 25.6% year on year to Rs 2.03 trillion ($21.40 billion) in October, according to a government statement reported by Reuters on Sunday.
  • Gross collection rose 22.9% to Rs 2.31 trillion, helped by a 42% jump in tax revenue from imports to Rs 72,246 crore, Business Standard reported.
  • Domestic GST revenue rose about 16% to over Rs 1.59 trillion, and refunds increased 6.5% to Rs 27,934 crore.
  • For NRIs watching the rupee and Indian markets, October was the fourth month of this financial year in which gross GST crossed Rs 2 trillion — a sign of sustained consumption and compliance, not a one-off spike.

India collected Rs 2.03 trillion ($21.40 billion) in net goods and services tax in October, up 25.6% from a year earlier, according to a government statement on Sunday reported by Reuters. Gross October collection stood at Rs 2.31 trillion, up 22.9%.

Imports did much of the heavy lifting

The detail behind the headline matters. Business Standard, reporting the same government data, said gross collection from domestic sales rose 16% to over Rs 1.59 trillion, while revenue from imports climbed 42% to Rs 72,246 crore. The gross total comprised Central GST of Rs 42,935 crore, State GST of Rs 51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over Rs 1.37 trillion.

Refunds rose 6.5% year on year to Rs 27,934 crore. After adjusting for refunds, net collection came to just over Rs 2.03 trillion — the 25.6% increase Reuters reported.

The seven-month picture

October was not an outlier. Business Standard reported that gross GST collection for April-October grew 13.2% to over Rs 14.77 trillion, with net collections up about 13% to over Rs 12.69 trillion. October was the fourth month of the financial year in which gross collection crossed Rs 2 trillion.

Two cautions belong with the celebration. First, import-linked tax revenue growing at 42% says as much about import values and enforcement at the border as it does about household demand. Second, these are nominal figures: they are not adjusted for inflation, so real growth is lower than the headline percentages.

What to watch next

The November print, due in early December, will show whether festive-season demand held after Diwali. For diaspora investors, the practical takeaway is narrower: sustained GST receipts above Rs 2 trillion a month support the government's fiscal position heading into the February budget, which is one input — not a guarantee — for rupee stability and Indian equity sentiment.
